title: Sovereign-fund megadeals needing US sign-off: PGA-PIF, EA, Aligned, G42
summary: Most links in the claim are documented, but the approvals behind them are often not. Trump hosted PGA Tour leaders and PIF governor Yasir Al-Rumayyan at the White House in February 2025, yet no PGA-PIF deal followed. PIF then said it would stop funding LIV after 2026, and LIV's new lead investor was still unnamed as of August 2026. The PGA Tour itself moved a $20M signature event to Trump Doral in 2026. EA's $55B buyout by PIF, Silver Lake and Kushner's Affinity closed on 4 Aug 2026, and press reports say all regulatory approvals, CFIUS included, came by 30 Jul 2026. No CFIUS decision or mitigation terms were made public. MGX's $40B Aligned purchase closed in July 2026, and no CFIUS outcome was reported. BIS moved the UAE to Country Group A:5 on 10 Jul 2026 and named G42 and Core42 for licence-free chip receipt. The report that G42 will reincorporate in the US rests on secondary relays of the WSJ, and on a Bloomberg report of 'exploratory talks' that G42 would not confirm. Lunate's takeover of G42's China fund is single-source (Bloomberg, 2024), and nothing later was found. Nothing shows that any approval was traded for family business.

sub_claims.statement: Trump personally brokered PGA Tour-PIF talks at the White House.
sub_claims.finding: DOCUMENTED (AP, ESPN, Golf Channel, Golf Digest). Monahan and Adam Scott met Trump at the White House on 2025-02-04, at the Tour's request. On 2025-02-20 Monahan, Tiger Woods and Scott held a session of about four hours with Trump and PIF governor Yasir Al-Rumayyan. The joint statement called it 'constructive' but announced no deal. The proposal under discussion was about $1.5B of PIF money into PGA Tour Enterprises, the same size as the investment by the US owners' group SSG. Golf Digest (March 2025) reported that the talks then stalled. Al-Rumayyan reportedly found the Tour's proposals inadequate. AP said that not even Trump could smooth the way. Brian Rolapp became PGA Tour CEO in mid-2025 and has since said there is 'no merger, no conversations' with LIV. The Justice Department's antitrust review of the 2023 framework agreement was the original approval hurdle. We found no 2025-26 DOJ decision. The Tour invited Trump in. He did not insert himself.

sub_claims.statement: While Trump was mediating, PIF-funded LIV played at Trump courses, and the PGA Tour also returned to Trump Doral.
sub_claims.finding: DOCUMENTED. The LIV events at Trump courses (Doral, April 2025; Trump National DC, May 2026; Bedminster, August 2026) are set out in C56. New here: the PGA Tour's Cadillac Championship was announced around 2025-12-15 and played at Trump National Doral on 2026-04-30 to 05-03. It is a $20M signature event, the Tour's first at Doral since 2016 (Fox Sports, NBC Sports, PGATour.com). Both sides of the dispute Trump was mediating therefore staged events at his family's resort within about a year. INFERRED: the observation that both parties became Trump Organization customers while he mediated is our own cross-reference. Host fees for both events are undisclosed, and no source ties the Doral choice to the talks.

sub_claims.statement: LIV has a new lead investor after PIF's exit, and that investor's identity is known.
sub_claims.finding: DOCUMENTED that PIF said around 2026-04-30 it would stop funding LIV after the 2026 season, having put in more than $5B since 2022, and that LIV appointed an independent board. On 2026-08-05 CEO Scott O'Neil announced a board-approved term sheet with an unnamed 'lead investor', with players to become majority equity holders and a close targeted for September 2026 (AP via Local10, Al Jazeera, Sky Sports, Golf Digest). We found no reporting that names the investor or confirms the close. Any link between the new investor and Trump, the Gulf funds or Affinity is therefore unknown, and we assert none.

sub_claims.statement: CFIUS handled the $55B EA buyout by PIF, Silver Lake and Kushner's Affinity.
sub_claims.finding: DOCUMENTED. The deal closed on 2026-08-04 at $210 a share and EA was delisted. Press reports, Gameluster among them, say the remaining regulatory approvals came by 2026-07-30, and some trade outlets say this was confirmed in an EA SEC filing that included CFIUS. The EU cleared the deal under merger rules on around 2026-07-23 and under its foreign-subsidies rules on around 2026-07-31. As late as July, the merger agreement's outside date (2026-09-28, extendable to 12-28) was described as hinging on CFIUS. SINGLE-SOURCE/UNVERIFIED: we found no Treasury statement and no public mitigation terms. An automated commentary site says no data firewall was disclosed. Treasury Secretary Bessent chairs CFIUS. The deal's critics are on record: Sens. Blumenthal and Warren (letter of 2025-10-14) wrote that the investors appear to be 'betting $1 billion that Mr. Kushner can deliver' approvals, and Lawfare (Vinita Singh, 2025-10-03) predicted 'the CFIUS review that will never be'. We could not access the primary SEC filing, so the CFIUS clearance rests on press accounts. Audit: GamingBolt, Mobilegamer.biz and Tech-Insider again report that EA's 30 Jul 2026 SEC filing said all required approvals were obtained, with CFIUS the last hurdle that pushed closing past the original 30 Jun target; ABC News (as relayed) gives 5 Aug rather than 4 Aug as the closing date. Still no Treasury statement or mitigation terms.

sub_claims.statement: MGX took part in the $40B Aligned Data Centers takeover with BlackRock/GIP, Nvidia and Microsoft, and it needed US approval.
sub_claims.finding: DOCUMENTED. Announced in October 2025: MGX, the AI Infrastructure Partnership (AIP, founded 2024 by BlackRock, GIP, MGX, Microsoft and Nvidia, with KIA and Temasek as anchor investors) and BlackRock's GIP would buy 100% of Aligned from Macquarie-managed funds for about $40B EV. The deal closed in July 2026 (The Next Web, 2026-07-21; DCD), with about $5B of extra growth capital. Aligned stays Dallas-based under CEO Andrew Schaap. At announcement, Data Center Frontier said a CFIUS review was expected. We found no report of a CFIUS filing, clearance or mitigation. So the approval process is UNVERIFIED, and the closing implies only that the parties' conditions were met. Tahnoon chairs MGX (C57).

sub_claims.statement: In 2026 the UAE got an export-control upgrade that named G42 for licence-free chips, after Tahnoon lobbied the White House.
sub_claims.finding: DOCUMENTED (BIS final rule, Skadden, Mondaq/Akin, Al-Monitor, Khaleej Times, DCD). BIS removed the UAE from Country Groups D:3/D:4 and added it to A:5, announced around 2026-07-10 and published in the Federal Register around 2026-07-14. Group 42 Holding (G42) and Core42 are listed in Supplement 8 to Part 740 as approved recipients of advanced-computing items without a licence, though not under License Exception STA. Their approval lapses after about 270 days, reported as around 2027-04-06, unless BIS extends it. Commerce said it would 'favorably review' MGX licence applications. Commerce cited UAE technology-protection measures and the UAE's support for the US in the 2026 Iran war. SINGLE-SOURCE (WSJ, relayed): Tahnoon led the lobbying and went directly to the White House after the war began. Sen. Warren (statement of 2026-07-10) called the rule a reward despite diversion risk and tied it to the Tahnoon-linked 49% stake in World Liberty. The White House and WLF deny any link. Audit: law-firm alerts (Latham, Skadden, Morgan Lewis, Akin, Steptoe) give the rule's effective date as 10 Jul 2026, and say the G42/Core42 approval expires on 6 Apr 2027 unless they become 'U.S. companies' or obtain approval via BIS's advisory-opinion process, which is the stated driver of the G42 restructuring talks in the next item. The Tahnoon lobbying account is still known only through relays of the WSJ.

sub_claims.statement: G42 is reincorporating as a US company.
sub_claims.finding: SINGLE-SOURCE and contested. A WSJ report from around July 2026, known only through aggregator relays (AI Weekly), said G42 plans to reincorporate as a US company owned mainly by US investors. Enterprise AM (2026-07-17) urged readers to take that 'with a kilo of salt'. Bloomberg (around 2026-09-04) reported only 'exploratory talks' about selling a majority stake to US companies or creating a new US vehicle. It said no decisions had been made and named no buyers. G42 declined to comment on 'confidential discussions'. Enterprise AM ran 'Will G42 become a US company?' in early November 2026, so the question was still open. The stated driver is the 270-day licence-free window in the BIS rule. Existing investors include Microsoft ($1.5B, 2024), Silver Lake and Mubadala.

sub_claims.statement: Lunate took over G42's China fund.
sub_claims.finding: SINGLE-SOURCE (Bloomberg, 2024-07-08, anonymous sources; Lunate declined to comment; widely relayed). Management of 42XFund passed from a G42 subsidiary to Lunate. 42XFund is a Shanghai-based growth fund launched in 2022 with about $10B and holding stakes in ByteDance and JD.com. Reports describe a change of manager, not a confirmed transfer of ownership. Bloomberg said this kept the assets inside Tahnoon's orbit. It came after G42 told the FT in February 2024 that it had divested its China holdings as part of the Microsoft deal. Bloomberg described Lunate as an IHC unit, while C57 records it as majority-owned by Chimera Investment; both are Tahnoon-linked. We found no 2025-26 follow-up on the fund. This needed no US approval, but it bears on whether G42 really split from China, a premise of every later US chip licence.

sub_claims.statement: Cross-deal connection: the same counterparties recur across these approvals and the Trump family's own deals.
sub_claims.finding: Each node is DOCUMENTED; the pattern is INFERRED (our cross-reference, asserted by no source). (1) Lunate, which took over G42's China fund, is also one of the three largest LPs in Kushner's Affinity (C15/C57). (2) Silver Lake sits in the EA buyout with Affinity, in the TikTok JV with MGX (C68) and on G42's cap table, so it has been co-investor with both the Kushner/PIF side and the Tahnoon side of three US-approval-dependent deals. (3) Microsoft and Nvidia co-own AIP, which bought Aligned with MGX, while Microsoft owns part of G42 and Nvidia sells chips under the UAE licences; both also funded Trump's ballroom (C68). (4) Tahnoon's MGX received 'favorable review' language in the same rule that freed G42, while his Aryam holds 49% of World Liberty (C57). The overlap shows that the same small set of capital pools needs, and receives, US decisions while also dealing with the family. It does not show coordination or exchange.

corrections: The claim says Trump was 'brokering' the PGA-PIF deal: the Tour asked him to join, the February 2025 sessions produced no agreement, and the talks later stalled. As of 2026 there is no PGA Tour-PIF deal.
The claim implies G42's US reincorporation has happened: only a relayed WSJ report and Bloomberg's 'exploratory talks' exist, and G42 has not confirmed either.
The 'takeover' of G42's China fund by Lunate was reported as a transfer of management (Bloomberg, 2024), not a confirmed change of ownership.
CFIUS clearance of EA rests on press accounts of an EA filing; no Treasury decision or mitigation agreement is public.
Some pages relaying golf coverage carry 2026 crawl-date banners on 2025 stories; an apparent 'October 2026' Trump-PGA-PIF meeting is a February 2025 article.
denials_and_context: The PGA Tour says it asked Trump to help. Monahan said Trump 'bolstered' the talks. Rolapp later disavowed a LIV merger.
PIF's exit from LIV and LIV's restructuring are commercial decisions. No source attributes them to US policy.
EA's buyers say the deal is a long-term investment, and Andrew Wilson remains CEO. Affinity's stake is about 1.1% (press estimate). Kushner holds no formal government role (C15).

Commerce justified the UAE upgrade by the UAE's security commitments and its support in the Iran war. The White House says the chip decisions are unrelated to Trump-family crypto business, and WLF denies any link.
G42 said it does not comment on confidential discussions. Lunate declined to comment on the China fund.
No CFIUS decisions are published by law. The absence of a public decision is normal and is not itself evidence of a skipped review.
